_about: SYNTHETIC intake notes only. Labels follow the intake spec rules and still need clinician sign-off. Expected stage is null when no stage should be given. Grow to 50 with pm-agent and engineer-agent.

cases.note: I'm Maya and I play soccer for my college team. Two weeks ago I went up for a header and collided with another player. The team doctor checked me that night. Now I get headaches by mid-afternoon, I feel foggy in lectures, and I'm more tired than usual. Screens bother me a little. Walking to class is fine, but when I tried a spin class the headache came back.
I hit my head at practice yesterday and I've thrown up three times since. When I look at my phone I'm seeing double.
I slipped on ice four days ago and hit the back of my head. My roommate says I had a seizure that night, though I don't remember it. I feel tired today.
Three days ago I hit my head on a car door. Today my headache is the worst it's been and keeps getting stronger, and I keep nodding off in the middle of conversations.
It's been three weeks since my concussion. I saw my doctor the first week. The headaches are a little better, but I feel hopeless and sometimes think everyone would be better off without me.
I fell off my bike this morning and bumped my head on the curb. I have a mild headache but otherwise I feel okay.
It's been ten days since I hit my head on a cabinet door. My brain fog and tiredness are getting worse every day, not better. I haven't seen anyone about it.

Three weeks ago I got a mild concussion skiing and saw my doctor the next day. I feel mostly back to normal, just a little tired at the end of the day. I've been jogging and lifting on my own without any problems.
My car accident was two months ago and my GP saw me that week. I still get a headache most afternoons and bright screens bother me. Walking around the neighborhood is fine.
I bumped my head on a shelf at work last week. I haven't seen a doctor. I've had a slight headache now and then but otherwise feel fine, and I walk my dog every day without any trouble.

Ten days ago I was hit in the head by a ball at my son's game. Urgent care checked me that day. My light sensitivity is so strong I can barely look at a screen, though walking outside with sunglasses is okay.

Five days ago I took a knee to the head at practice. I didn't pass out and I haven't thrown up. My sports medicine doctor saw me the next day. I have a mild headache in the evenings, and I've been jogging on my own with no problems.
cases.note_for_reviewers: Known keyword false alarm: the backup scan fires on 'pass out' and 'thrown up' even when negated. Kept so the eval shows the cost.
